g.text: Installs an older Linux Steam client from a Wayback Machine snapshot (or SteamTracking) into
`force-wayback TS` · fetch-smart, read the build id, then destructive install
`status.py` · build id, overlay md5, update lock, running clients, per-cache completeness
`cache/<buildid>/` · manifest + roughly 500 MB of blobs per build, gitignored
`~/.steam/debian-installation/package/` · the blobs the Steam bootstrap is allowed to extract
`logs/bootstrap_log.txt` · the "Update complete" line apply_mirror greps for
`client-update.fastly.steamstatic.com` · live CDN, same client file names
`/usr/games/steam` · the real bootstrap: reads package/ + mirror, extracts, writes the log
`pgrep` / `pkill` · refuses, or kills, while a client is still up
`fetch_smart.py` · Wayback first, SteamTracking fill on failure
`nuke_client.py` · back up client trees, then delete them
`vzip.py` · Valve `.vz`: LZMA1 body, CRC32 + size footer
same install step, one fetch in front
the manifest decides what to download
smart only adds a fallback source
the fallback is a SteamTracking commit lookup
mirror runs as a child for the one forced update
a replaced stub is what verify checks for
a complete cache is the precondition for wiping anything
the extract can leave a bootstrap-era stub
manifests and blobs come back with a build id
